_about: Ambient NPC dialogue (DialogueBank). Per area, per NPC id: an ORDERED list of variants -- the first whose 'if' passes plays. 'if' is a story condition: after('flag'), before('flag'), has('flag'), flag('x') >= 2, visited('area'), rests_since('flag') >= 3, steps_since('flag') >= 200, minutes_since('flag') >= 10; blank = always. Line speakers: self, hero, narrator or another NPC id of the area. Edit with the Dialogue editor (Godot: the 'Dialogue' main-screen tab) or by hand; no rebuild, no save migration. Cutscenes stay in game/overworld/build/build_story_content.gd.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Starstone buns, half price! ...Nobody's buying starstone anything this week. They're currant buns now. Very loyal currant buns.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Starstone buns! Get your starstone buns! ...No, there's no starstone in them. There's currants. Glowing currants would be a health hazard.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Biscuit presses against your legs and will not let go. It has not left Brisa's side since the raid.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Petalfang sniffs your hand and wags its whole back half.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: If they took the Researcher for his shards... then everyone who carries one is a target now. Keep yours hidden, {hero}.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I was in the first batch of testers! Biscuit here trusted me the moment the shard warmed. You'll see -- it feels like a second heartbeat.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Cindral raiders, they're saying. Funny -- Cindral has no shards of its own. So why come all this way for the man who makes them?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: A select few testers, and a crate for the army. Everyone else keeps waiting. That's how it always goes, isn't it?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Turnips are selling again. Folk are frightened, but frightened folk still eat. Nothing comforts like a stew.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Raiders, in the royal city! In broad daylight! What's next -- dragons in the fish stall?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Everyone wants to talk shards today. Nobody wants to buy turnips. You'd think a bit of glowing rock was worth more than supper.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Black chains on those raider beasts, they're saying. BLACK. Starstone forged that way was outlawed before my father was born.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Somebody has been keeping old secrets. Mark me.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: In my father's day, the lords bound their creatures in chains -- starstone chains, forged hot. The beasts obeyed. They never loved anyone for it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Good folk did it the slow way: years of trust, trial and error, bread and patience. Those bonds need no shard at all.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Now the Researcher says almost anyone can do it with a sliver of the same stone. Hm. Stone is stone. It's the hand that holds it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Spearheads. Shield rims. Every blade the Guard owns passes under my hammer this week. Whoever did this is going to regret it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Forged half the spears on those walls. The other half I'm still forging. Ask the Guard -- they never have enough spears.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Gates shut at dusk now, and every cart gets turned out. Orders from the keep. Don't take it personally.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Crownhaven's gates are open from dawn to dusk. Keep the peace inside them.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The west road is open again. Through the Sparse Forest, and Woodland Town's at the far side of it -- keep to the cart ruts, and don't follow any lights.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The west gate stays barred today. Orders from the keep -- nobody in, nobody out.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The Cindral envoy went in an hour ago. I haven't heard shouting yet. Give it time.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The King is in council. No petitions today.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The King is in council with his war lords. No petitions -- not today, not this week.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The King is in council. No petitions today.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Mum says I can go past the fountain again! I went past it twice, to make sure.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Mum says I'm not allowed past the fountain till the soldiers catch them.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I saw an officer's Geode this morning! It was THIS big. Bigger! When I'm a tester I'm getting two.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Word from the border: Cindral's mustering too. Everyone's preparing for war.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The Guard's on alert till the King decides what this raid means. I think it means war.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The army got a crate of the Researcher's shards last month. Only the officers carry them. An officer's Geode could flatten this dummy with one arm.

lyra.note: Waiting by the south gate after the opening, until the first rival duel (the duel itself is offered when you talk to her -- the builder's Lyra script). TODO(story): rewritten when Lark was merged into Lyra.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Well? Ready to test each other?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Half my rooms are full of frightened scholars and the other half of soldiers. The kitchen's never been so busy -- and I've never been so worried.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Welcome to the Stag! Testers from every corner of Aldermere sleep under this roof the night before the ceremony. Nobody sleeps well, mind.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: If you're heading for the forest, the Wardens at Woodland Town keep a good table. Tell them Maribel sent you -- they'll water the soup.

merchant.note: Merchant Oda: this is her greeting; the shop opens after it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Still open, love -- raid or no raid. I'd stock up on tonics, the way things are going.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Welcome to the market! Tonics for the road, salves for the stings -- have a look.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The council has argued for three days. Chancellor Vesk would have us at war by the harvest.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I prefer the garden. The garden has never once wanted a war.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The King will not see petitioners, but the garden is lovely this time of year. Please admire it quietly.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The Mountain Road's shut tighter than ever. Half the garrison at Mountain Base is being called down. Something's coming.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The Mountain Road's shut. Supply wagons for the garrison at Mountain Base go up under escort, and nobody else goes up at all.

odalys.note: TODO(story): the default line is a neutral placeholder (the fallen-star / shard lore it used to repeat is not decided).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I lit a candle for the Researcher.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Welcome to the chapel, traveller. Be gentle with what you bond.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: They came over the EAST wall, and out through my gate before I'd got my spear up. I'll not forget it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: A shard tester, from Oakvale? The Researcher's workshop is in the upper town -- east of the keep. Mind the market crowd.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: They knew exactly where he'd be, and exactly when. They didn't touch a single note -- they only wanted HIM.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Don't touch the pylon, please. The last tester who touched the pylon could hear colours for a week.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The raid has done what no bandit ever managed: shut the King's own road. Every caravan searched twice over.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I used to dislike closed roads. I find I have graduated to loathing them.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Five gates, five roads, and every merchant on them answers to this hall.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Timber from Woodland Town, grain from Oakvale, iron from Mountain Base, salt fish from Beach Village, red clay from the Badlands -- when the roads are open. Most are closed. I dislike closed roads.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: You came all the way from Woodland Town? Through the trees?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Welcome to Deepwood. Our chief lives in the lodge to the north-east.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The forest gets thicker the deeper you go. Watch the grass.

lyra.note: TODO(story): placeholder lines (DECISIONS.md #88: Lyra is met here and joins the Eldroot battle).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The trail north is open. When you face what's in the deepest part of the wood, I'll fight beside you.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: {hero}! You came to Deepwood too. Something waits in the deepest part of the forest -- when you go, I'm coming with you.

bram.note: A trainer: the bank is only consulted once he is BEATEN (his challenge stays in the builder).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Off to get stronger before the war, I hear. Then I'll keep the grass honest while you're gone. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Hah... you'll do. Whatever you're chasing, I hope you catch it.

fenna.note: A trainer: the bank is only consulted once she is BEATEN.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: You've duelled Lyra? Professor Elias' student, that one. My Petalfang wants a rematch with you first, mind.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Well fought. My Petalfang's sulking now -- that means you earned it.

nell.note: Only on the planks while the ambush is sprung (visible_if).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Still here? Then your purse is still ours.

pedlar.note: Merchant: this is his greeting; the shop opens after it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: You're the one who sent Nell's lot packing? The road's twice as busy since. Good for trade -- have a look, friend.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Mind the grass, traveller. Need anything for the road?

briony.note: The hero's mother. Oakvale (home) only exists before the raid.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Back already? Don't tell me the city turned you round at the gate.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Go on -- Professor Elias is waiting for you at his workshop.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: East along the Mossway to River Crossing, then north over the Old Bridge -- Crownhaven's south gate is at the end of it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Go on -- Professor Elias is an old friend of the family. Don't keep him waiting.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The soldiers rode back through at noon, dusty and quiet. Whatever they went to the border to see, they didn't like it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Soldiers went down the Mossway at dawn, riding for the border. Nobody would say why.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: There's talk of Cindral again. There's always talk of Cindral.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Stew's on, and the hearth's lit. Travellers stop here before the Mossway -- it's a long road to River Crossing, and a longer one to the city.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Folk say the old bridge at River Crossing is older than the kingdom. Mind the toll-keeper; he'll tell you the same story twice.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Forty harvests I've brought in off that field. A good year's barley for the bread, a bad year's for the pigs.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: This year the creatures in the hedgerow have been restless. Something stirs them. Mind yourself out there.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Did you see the King? Did he have his crown ON? Was it heavy? Did you ask him if it was heavy?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Will your creature be big? Will it breathe fire? Can I hold the shard? Just once?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: You've been to the capital already? Is it true every street is paved in stone? EVERY one?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Then what do they do with all their mud?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Off to get your shard, then? Pa says in his day you befriended a creature by sharing your bread with it for a year.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Less bread this way, I suppose.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I'm watching the pond for the golden frog. Nobody's seen it. That's how I know it's clever.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Maud's walking again, a little, with a stick Ned cut for her. She asks for your mother every morning, and every morning I have to tell her.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: We laid her beside the house she built. Every one of the little ones put a flower on the cairn.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: She'd want you to go, {hero}.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Go and find Professor Elias, and bring him home.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I'm so sorry, {hero}.

marra.note: Out in the ruins only after the opening (visible_if).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Rafters are up! Farm Hamlet's timber, Oakvale's hands. Come back in a month and I'll have a door. Maybe even a bed.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The Hearth & Hen burned to the hearthstone. The hearthstone's still good, though. We'll have a roof on it by the harvest -- Farm Hamlet's sending timber.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: You'll always have a bowl of stew here, {hero}. Even if for now it's stew under the sky.

ned.note: Out in the ruins only after the opening (visible_if).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Turned the ash into the soil this morning. My back says it was a mistake. My barley will say otherwise, come spring.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Forty harvests off that field, and the forty-first is ash. Ash is good for the soil, mind. Next year's barley will be the best this village ever grew.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I'm going to be a tester when I'm big. A real one. And I'm never hiding in a cellar again.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: ...She told us to count to a thousand in the dark and not come out. I only got to four hundred.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Farm Hamlet's timber came in yesterday. The first new roof goes on the Hearth & Hen -- Marra's orders, and nobody argues with Marra.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Any word of Professor Elias? ...No. I didn't think so. Keep looking, {hero}.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: We'll rebuild. Oakvale always does. Go and find the ones who did this, {hero}.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: And bring Professor Elias home.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: They went past the mill toward the border. The General's waiting on you.

wick.note: Out in the ruins only after the opening (visible_if).

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I've named the golden frog Briony. Is that alright? It seemed like a brave sort of name.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The golden frog came back to the pond this morning. I saw it. It means the village is going to be alright.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Still no word of the Researcher? I've had soldiers over this bridge every day since. Going north, mostly. Always north.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: This bridge is older than the kingdom, you know. It's seen wars start before. It never liked it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Raiders came over my bridge at a dead run, red cloaks, a man in a scholar's coat slung between them. Didn't stop. Didn't pay.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Forty years I've kept this bridge. Never seen anyone cross it like they were running from the city instead of to it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Welcome to the Old Bridge! Older than the kingdom, this bridge. The first King of Aldermere rode over it to his crowning -- and paid the toll, mind.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Testers carrying the Researcher's letter cross free, by royal order. Everyone else, a copper. The bridge doesn't mind either way.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Did I tell you this bridge is older than the kingdom? The first King rode over it to his crowning. Paid the toll, too.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Coast road's still washed out, and now there's soldiers on the King's road turning out every cart. I'll be stuck here so long they'll make me a local.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Coast road's washed out past the ford. Beach Village will have to wait for its flour, and I'll have to wait for Beach Village.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: They say the harbour's full of ships bound for the isles, and none of them able to sail till the road's mended. Funny old world.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: They forded the shallows below the bridge, the raiders -- churned the whole bed to mud. Fish won't bite since. Can't say I blame them.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The river comes down from the city walls and runs out to the sea past Beach Village. Every fish in it has seen the King. Not one of them is impressed.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I dropped a pebble off the bridge and wished for the soldiers to catch the bad men. That's forty-one wishes. I'm owed.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: If you drop a pebble off the bridge and count to three, a river spirit grants you a wish. I've wished for a creature forty times.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Soldiers on the west road, heading for the woods. Tell them to keep their boots off my saplings.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Sparse, they call it. Sparse! Every tree you see here, my grandfather planted, and every tree you don't, he cut. It's a garden, really.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: West of the town the woods close up for good -- the Deep Woods. Nobody plants those. Nobody cuts them, either.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Back again? The pie's the same, the cider's the same, and the odd crowd's still asking about the south trail. Some things in this town never change.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Venison pie, hot cider, and a room with a window onto the pines. The Stumped Hart's never let a traveller go hungry.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Odd crowd lately. Folk with no luggage and a lot of questions about the south trail. I tell them it's a trail to nowhere.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Axe heads, saw teeth, nails by the barrel. The Guard's smiths in the city make swords. I make the things that actually feed people.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Forty-two lanterns last night! And STILL only forty windows. I'm keeping a list now.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I counted forty-one lanterns last night and only forty windows. Nobody believes me.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Three arrows, three straw men, and one of them is still standing. Don't ask which. The range is open to anyone who can keep from shooting the pigeons.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The Deepwood road's open to you. Keep to the track, and mind the wood.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Word is Crownhaven's preparing for war, and you with it. Then you're welcome at this Lodge at any hour.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Welcome to Woodland Town. The Wardens keep the roads, the tolls and the peace between the town and the trees -- in about that order of difficulty.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Deepwood's road is shut. The wood's been restless, and a restless wood eats carts. If you want to go west, bring me a reason I can write down.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: And if you meet a lantern in the dark that nobody's holding -- go the other way.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Bitterroot for stings, mossleaf for scrapes, and something I'm not allowed to call a cure for anything at all. Don't tell the Wardens.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The woods are older than the kingdom, you know. Things sleep in the roots out there. Nobody here says so aloud.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: East road's clear to the city. If anyone asks, I wasn't smiling.

sedge.note: Merchant: this is his greeting; the shop opens after it.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Furs, flasks and forest remedies, friend. Have a look.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Taking up with the Crown's soldiers now? Pity. You had a face for doors and exits.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Warm fire, warm night. You've the look of someone who counts doors and exits, traveller. Good habit.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Some doors in this wood are only doors if you know the knock. I'd tell you the knock, but I don't know it. Obviously.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Every plank in the capital's keep started life on this yard. Mind the stacks -- they have opinions about strangers.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: We only fell what's marked. The Wardens paint a ring on the trunk, and I don't argue with a ring.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: When I was a girl this stone was taller. Or I was shorter. The glade keeps its own counsel.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: If you're ever lost in the woods, set your hand on a stone and listen. The star remembers the way home.
